group:paper-mock-jiangsu-nantong-2026-01.overview: 文章鼓励读者与同龄人分享自己的经历，指出经历不分大小都有价值，并给出三条建议：讲清细节、站在听者角度解释用词、勇敢说出自己的看法。
group:paper-mock-jiangsu-nantong-2026-01.fullTranslationZh:
分享是我们日常生活中必不可少的一部分。当你和同龄人分享自己的经历时，他们会更愿意放心地分享自己的经历。分享对你重要的事情，没有任何限制。如果你觉得自己没有什么大的经历可讲，分享经历的念头因此让你望而却步，那就马上克服它，因为所有的经历都同样有价值。下面是让你的分享更有效的几条建议。
分享细节。一定要讲得尽可能详细。试着把你的经历描绘给别人看，让他们也能感同身受。告诉他们你有什么感受，以及为什么会有这样的感受。先讲你是什么时候想到要分享这件事的，再讲发生了什么或者你当时是怎么想的。最后讲讲它为什么对你很重要，或者你为什么会这样想。
解释用词。从别人的角度想一想这个问题。如果你来自另一个群体，你能听懂你所说的每一个词吗？如果不能，就考虑解释一下其中的术语。比如，不要对来自世界各地的同龄人说：“我喜欢卡塔卡利，你以后一定要去看看。”而要这样说：“我喜欢卡塔卡利，它是一种民间舞蹈，舞者戴着独特的面具表演一出戏剧。你以后应该去看看。”
无所畏惧。分享经历时，你不必难为情，也不必害怕敞开心扉。你完全有权利勇敢而坦率。例如，假设你们在讨论性别平等，有些同龄人认为女性只能从事某些职业，而你不同意。那么，不要担心自己说出与众不同的观点后别人会怎么想，直接说出来就好。
既然你已经读了我关于分享的建议，那就去和世界上其他人分享你自己的经历、想法和思考吧。记住，经历没有太大或太小之分。所有的经历都有各自的价值。无论你分享什么，对于经历和你不同、看法和你不同的人来说，都会是独特而新鲜的。所以，继续分享吧。

selectedLongSentences.sourceText: If the thought of sharing your experiences holds you back because you believe that you don’t have big experiences to share, then, you should get over it right away because all experiences are equally valuable.
selectedLongSentences.displayText: If the thought of sharing your experiences holds you back because you believe that you don’t have big experiences to share, then, you should get over it right away because all experiences are equally valuable.
selectedLongSentences.translationZh: 如果你觉得自己没有什么大的经历可讲，分享经历的念头因此让你望而却步，那就马上克服它，因为所有的经历都同样有价值。
selectedLongSentences.analysisZh: 主干在 then 后面：you should get over it right away（你应该马上克服它）。前面 If 引导条件从句，主语是 the thought of sharing your experiences（分享经历的念头），谓语是 holds you back；从句里又套一个 because 从句说明退缩的原因，其中 that 从句作 believe 的宾语。主句的 it 指这个让人退缩的念头，句末第二个 because 给出应当克服它的理由。

underlineRanges.quote: you should get over it right away
because all experiences are equally valuable

selectedLongSentences.sourceText: Then, instead of fearing what people would think if you said something unconventional, just say it.
selectedLongSentences.displayText: Then, instead of fearing what people would think if you said something unconventional, just say it.
selectedLongSentences.translationZh: 那么，不要担心自己说出与众不同的观点后别人会怎么想，直接说出来就好。
selectedLongSentences.analysisZh: 主干是祈使句 just say it（直接说出来）。前面 instead of 是介词，后面接动名词 fearing，表示「不去担心」；fearing 的宾语是 what 引导的从句 what people would think，从句里再带 if you said something unconventional，用 said 和 would think 表示假设的情况：万一你说了与众不同的话，别人会怎么想。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按「提出观点 → 分条建议 → 总结号召」展开：首段说分享重要、经历不论大小都值得讲，并引出建议；中间三段各以一个祈使句小标题开头，分别讲细节、用词和勇气；末段回到经历不分大小，号召继续分享。

units.summary: 分享能让同伴也敞开心扉；不必因为觉得经历不够大而退缩，所有经历都同样有价值，下面给出建议。

units.heading: Share the details.
units.summary: 第一条建议：把经历讲细，讲出感受和原因，并按想法产生、事情经过、为何重要的顺序讲。

units.heading: Explain the words.
units.summary: 第二条建议：站在来自其他群体的听者角度，解释他们可能听不懂的术语，并举介绍卡塔卡利舞的例子。

units.heading: Be fearless.
units.summary: 第三条建议：分享时不必害怕，有不同意见就直接说出来，并以讨论性别平等为例。
总结：经历不分大小，各有价值，对不同的人都新鲜，鼓励读者继续分享。

B.text: 选项和原文没有共用的词，只是用感叹语气肯定某件事成立，像在呼应全文「经历都有价值」。最接近的是第 40 题：it 只能指空前的 experience，但空前 "no experience is too big or too small" 用的是 is，does 找不到可替代的动作，句子说不通。
quotes: no experience is too big or too small

C.text: 选项和 "Explain the words."、"Be fearless." 一样是祈使句，又和空后 "picturise your experience for others" 都说经历，放第 37 题段首很像。但空后 "as much detail as possible" 要的是把细节讲给别人，不是自己理清经历。放进第 38 题也接不上：make sense 像空后的 understand，可 "if you were from another community" 要的是换位想听者。
quotes: if you were from another community

completedSourceTexts.text: Sharing is an essential part of our daily lives. When you share your experiences with your peers, they are more likely to feel comfortable sharing their own. There are no restrictions on sharing what matters to you. If the thought of sharing your experiences holds you back because you believe that you don’t have big experiences to share, then, you should get over it right away because all experiences are equally valuable. Here are the tips to make your sharing experience more effective.

Share the details. Make sure that you go into as much detail as possible. Try to picturise your experience for others so that they can just feel like you do. Share with them what you feel and why you feel that way. Start by sharing when you had the idea for what you are sharing. Then share what happened or what you thought. After that, share why it is important to you or why you think the way you do.

Explain the words. Think about this from another person’s perspective. Would you understand every word of your dialogue if you were from another community? If not, consider defining the jargon（术语）. As an alternative to saying to your global peers, “I love Kathakali and you should definitely watch it someday.” Say something like: “I love Kathakali, which is a form of folk dance, in which the dancers present a drama wearing unique masks. You should watch it someday.”

Be fearless. While sharing an experience, you do not have to be embarrassed, afraid to open up. You have every right to be brave and frank. For example, suppose you are discussing gender equality, and some of your peers support the idea that women can only work in certain professions, and you disagree with them. Then, instead of fearing what people would think if you said something unconventional, just say it.

Now that you have read my tips for sharing, go share your own experiences, ideas, and thoughts with the rest of the world. Remember that no experience is too big or too small. All experiences matter in their own way. Whatever you share would be unique and new to someone who has had different experiences or has different perspectives from you. So, continue to share.
